task: Stabilize local story owner identity across shell boundaries without collapsing independent tasks or agents.
outcome: The same host task and agent can invoke Lattice through different shell parent processes without a false foreign-owner rejection; a different task or agent remains rejected, and degraded ppid identity is clearly diagnosed.
facts: Core ownership consumes a resolved session identity and currently falls back to hostname+root+ppid.
Canonical documents require LATTICE_SESSION_ID as the only generic core owner id and keep provider-specific signals at adapter boundaries.
The accepted Workstream D contract requires a composite taskIdentity + agentOrRoleIdentity; repository-global and thread-only identities are rejected.

Codex, Claude, and agy launchers are installed, but the current parent environment exposes no native stable session variables; supported adapters/wrappers must inject validated dimensions or a bounded generated boundary.
Owner leases are local non-cryptographic write-coordination metadata; takeover semantics remain unchanged.

Fresh initial Codex and Antigravity/agy reviews passed over the pre-update document, but they will not authorize runtime after the canonical document changes; fresh post-document reviews are required.
Claude evidence was excluded because permission, binding, and liveness failures prevented one exact valid PASS.
constraints: Do not use a repo-global token that collapses independent tasks.
Do not collapse implementer, verification-intent, reviewer, or other agent/role identities within one task.
Do not treat the local identity as authentication, Authority evidence, or reviewer independence proof.
Keep explicit LATTICE_SESSION_ID highest priority and derived-ppid only as a visible degraded fallback.
Persisted generated tokens must be registered runtime artifacts, gitignored, excluded from material hashes, and have bounded cleanup.
Keep lease equality and takeover state-machine semantics unchanged.
No raw host-native token may be logged or persisted as review/story prose.
Update the canonical document and refresh two-host review plus the three manual transcripts before any runtime implementation.
